style_1_icd10.name: Diabetes insipidus
style_1_icd10.chapter: IV. Endocrine, nutritional and metabolic diseases (E00-E89)

style_2_guidelines.guideline_authority: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes (2024) / EASD Consensus
steps_summary: Stage 1: First-Line Therapy: Foundation & Organ Protection
Stage 2: Second-Line / Dual Add-On Therapy (HbA1c Above Goal)
Stage 3: Third-Line & Injectable Therapy (Severe Hyperglycemia / Target Not Met)
pearls: Contraindicated if eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73m². Reduce dose by 50% if eGFR 30–44. Check vitamin B12 levels periodically.
Demonstrated major reductions in cardiovascular death, HF hospitalization, and CKD progression. Advise genital hygiene and adequate hydration.
Potent HbA1c reduction and weight loss. Avoid in personal/family history of Medullary Thyroid Carcinoma or MEN 2.

special_populations.renal_impairment: Metformin: safe down to eGFR 45; max 1000 mg/day if eGFR 30–44; stop if eGFR < 30. SGLT2i (Dapagliflozin/Empagliflozin): maintain down to dialysis for cardiorenal protection (glycemic effect diminishes below eGFR 45). Linagliptin requires no dose adjustment across all stages of CKD.
special_populations.hepatic_impairment: Avoid Metformin in severe hepatic impairment (lactic acidosis risk). Pioglitazone contraindicated if active liver disease/ALT > 3x ULN.
special_populations.pregnancy_lactation: Insulin is the standard of care during pregnancy. Oral agents are generally discontinued.

style_3_monograph.summary: Diabetes insipidus (DI) causes frequent urination. You become extremely thirsty, so you drink. Then you urinate. This cycle can keep you from sleeping or even make you wet the bed. Your body produces lots of urine that is almost all water. DI is different from diabetes mellitus (DM), which involves insulin problems and high blood sugar. The symptoms can be similar. However, DI is related to how your kidneys handle fluids. It's much less common than DM. Urine and blood tests can show which one you have. Usually, DI is caused by a problem with your pituitary gland or your kidneys. Treatment depends on the cause of the problem. Medicines can often help. NIH: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases
style_3_monograph.treatment: Consult healthcare provider for individualized management.

approved_molecules.name: CARBAMAZEPINE
